speaker: Doctor
text: I understand you are presenting with swelling in your right knee and a history of similar issues in your family. To begin our assessment, have you experienced any pain, clicking, or instability in the joint, and can you describe what activities typically trigger these symptoms?

speaker: Patient
text: 18-month-old boy. The patient is brought in by his parents due to swelling in his right knee noticed after playing in the park. The parents report that there was no obvious injury or incident at the park that could have led to the swelling. Upon further questioning, the mother recalls that an uncle on her side of the family had similar problems, suggesting a possible genetic component.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Osteochondritis dissecans (OCD). Given the patient's age (18 months), spontaneous swelling without trauma, and the strong familial history, this clinical picture is highly suggestive of a genetic predisposition to OCD, likely involving a mutation in the COL2A1 gene or a similar connective tissue disorder affecting cartilage integrity.
